record.context_brief: Finite powers in the Borel case
record.original_question: Is any of the three Borel-cover classes S_1(B_Ω, B_Γ), S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), or S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) closed under taking finite powers of a space?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2 ([47, Problem 50]). Is any of the classes S1(BΩ, BΓ), S1(BΩ, BΩ), or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) closed under taking finite powers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a topological space. A cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ by proper subsets is called an $\omega$-cover if every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$, and a $\gamma$-cover if $\mathcal{U}$ is infinite and every point of $X$ belongs to all but finitely many members of $\mathcal{U}$. Let $B_\Omega(X)$ denote the family of all countable Borel $\omega$-covers of $X$, and let $B_\Gamma(X)$ denote the family of all countable Borel $\gamma$-covers of $X$.

For families $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ of covers of $X$, define the following selection principles:
- $S_1(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{A}$, there exist $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}\in\mathcal{B}$.
- $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{A}$, there exist finite $\mathcal{F}_n\subseteq\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_n\mathcal{F}_n\in\mathcal{B}$.

Say that a class $\Pi$ of topological spaces is closed under taking finite powers if $X\in\Pi$ implies $X^n\in\Pi$ for every positive integer $n$.

Question: Is any of the three classes
$$S_1(B_\Omega,B_\Gamma),\quad S_1(B_\Omega,B_\Omega),\quad S_{\mathrm{fin}}(B_\Omega,B_\Omega)$$
(viewed as the class of spaces $X$ satisfying the corresponding principle) closed under taking finite powers?
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that this problem (Problem 50 in Tsaban's "Selection principles in mathematics: A milestone of open problems") was answered affirmatively by Sakai, as a consequence of his negative answer to a related problem. Thus all three Borel-cover classes are known to be closed under finite powers.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles in mathematics: A milestone of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Sakai showed that the answer for Problem 24 is No, and this also answers Problem 50 in the affirmative.
status_evidence.claim: Problem 50, asking whether the three Borel-cover classes are closed under finite powers, is answered in the affirmative by Sakai's work.
